conviction_note: Near-balanced. Two negatives: the Q3 rate shock to fair-value loan marks (2-5y Treasuries up 74-90bp against 27-35bp in Q2, when personal-loan marks fell 71bp), and the second-half ramp the unchanged $0.60 FY EPS guide needs ($0.24 in H1, so $0.36 in H2). Both agree with a +10.5 put skew, KBW published the first one around Oct 14, and the stock is at a 52-week low. Against them: short interest of 17% of float and rising, the October rate reversal that helps the Q4 guide, and benign peer credit. The findings sum to +0.3 and the scaled number is -0.36 (p_up 48, abs 9.0). The two disagree in sign and both are small, so this is a coin flip with a large absolute move.
bar: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS $0.17 and revenue about $1.25B. Investing.com preview of 2026-10-26 (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/sofi-earnings-on-deck-as-analysts-clash-on-capital-concerns-93CH-4973016) and the Benzinga consensus table (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/SOFI/earnings-forecasts: $0.16-0.17, $1.25-1.26B) agree to within a cent. Company FY2026 guide from the Q2 8-K of 2026-07-29 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001818874/000181887426000050/a2026q2earningsrelease.htm): adjusted net revenue $4.75-4.85B, adjusted EBITDA about $1.6B, adjusted net income about $825M, adjusted EPS about $0.60 at a 22% tax rate, members +30% or more. No Q3 quarterly guide was given (Q2 call transcript, https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1978081-20260808). Consensus Q3 EPS of $0.17 is 40% above Q2's actual $0.12.
positioning_check: Short interest 214,897,462 shares, 17.07% of float, 4.2 days to cover, up 13.71% from 188,982,888 at the prior settlement. Record date 2026-09-30, FINRA publication 2026-10-09 (MarketBeat, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/SOFI/short-interest/). For comparison, MarketBeat put it at 9.28% of float in October 2025. This is a crowded and building short. Baseline: 25-delta skew +10.54 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.59, event-implied move 8.51%, spot $14.53, 54.9% below the 52-week high and 2.2% above the 52-week low, 20-day run-up -8.79%. Sell-side targets were cut into the print: Truist $19 to $16 (Oct 23), KBW Underperform at $15, Goldman Hold $18 to $15, TD Cowen $18 to $17.50. StoneX initiated at Buy, $25.

findings.finding: The Q3 rate shock on SoFi's fair-value loan book was about 2.5 times Q2's. On the Treasury par curve, June 30 to September 30, 2026: 2y 4.14% to 4.88% (+74bp), 3y 4.15% to 5.00% (+85bp), 5y 4.19% to 5.09% (+90bp). In Q2 the same tenors rose 27-35bp (March 31: 3.79/3.81/3.92) and personal-loan marks still fell 71bp to 104.7%. About $46.7B of loans are carried at fair value (10-Q, June 30, 2026), so the Q3 mark-down before hedges is plausibly several hundred million dollars, against a quarterly adjusted net revenue bar of about $1.25B. Hedge offsets are not disclosed in anything I could read.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 and Q2 2026 both carried rate-driven mark-downs (Q1 benchmark +31bp, Q2 personal-loan marks -71bp) and both still beat revenue (Q2 $1.21B against $1.11B). The stock fell 15.4% after Q1 and 8.9% after Q2 on guidance and profit, not on the marks themselves.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. KBW (Switzer) put the Q3 headwind from rates and balance-sheet growth at more than $1B before hedges, around mid-October (TIKR, 2026-10-16), and the stock made a 52-week low on Oct 14-15 with a +10.5 put skew. If it were fully priced, consensus revenue would have been cut. It was not: Investing.com reports revisions over the past week of +0.57% on revenue and +0.67% on EPS, and KBW itself still expects consensus to be met. The size of the net hit after hedges is the part nobody has quantified.
findings.independence: Proxy finding: macro-to-company transmission that the company has not confirmed. KBW's estimate (https://www.tikr.com/it/blog/sofi-stock-hit-a-52-week-low-on-october-15-heres-what-the-october-27-report-has-to-settle) points the same way from a different source. Q2 mark and balances come from the Q2 8-K and 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1818874/000181887426000054/sofi-20260630.htm). Shares its mechanism (profit pressure from rates) with the guidance-ramp finding, but rests on a different fact.

findings.finding: The unchanged FY2026 guide of about $825M adjusted net income and about $0.60 adjusted EPS needs a steep second half. H1 adjusted net income was $327.1M ($0.24 a share; Q2 $160.4M, $0.12), so H2 needs about $498M, or about $0.18 a quarter, which is 50% above Q2's run-rate. Q3 consensus of $0.17 already assumes most of that ramp. The guide was set assuming one or two Fed hikes, and Q3 delivered a September hike plus an 85bp shift in the 3-5y part of the curve. Holding $0.60 is a stretch; cutting it repeats the April and July pattern (EPS guide not raised, stock down).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 29, 2026: revenue guide raised to $4.75-4.85B with EBITDA and EPS held, and the stock fell 8.9% (baseline; Reuters via TIKR blamed the unchanged profit outlook). April 29, 2026: the stock fell 15.4% on guidance described as underwhelming despite a revenue beat.
findings.why_not_priced: The arithmetic is public, so it is mostly priced through the 55% drawdown and the skew. What is not priced is whether management reaffirms or cuts the profit guide after a quarter of rates well above its own assumption. Consensus at $0.17 for Q3 (+40% quarter on quarter) shows the street has not marked the ramp down. If it had, Q3 EPS estimates would sit near $0.13-0.14.
findings.independence: Fed hike and rates context: Treasury par curve (finding 1) and the Q2 call, where the CFO set out the 1-2 hike assumption and the 22% tax rate (https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1978081-20260808). Shares the profit-under-rates mechanism with finding 1. Not double-counted: one finding is the reported-quarter mark, the other is the full-year guide.

findings.finding: Rates retraced in October, which gives management room to hold the Q4 and FY guide. By October 23 the par curve was 2y 4.69% (from 4.88% on Sep 30), 3y 4.75% (from 5.00%), 5y 4.82% (from 5.09%) and 10y 5.00% (from 5.29%), so quarter-to-date marks have partly recovered. SoFi can cite this on the call as support for Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean precedent in the baseline. In 2025, when rates eased, prints were rewarded (+6.6% Jul-25, +5.5% Oct-25).
findings.why_not_priced: Previews focus on the Q3 headwind (KBW, Goldman, Truist all cut targets on rates in October) and none I found mentions the quarter-to-date reversal. If the market were pricing a Q4 tailwind, the October target cuts and the put skew would not have widened into the print. The FOMC on Oct 27-28 is a coin flip between a hike and a hold (TIKR), which caps this.
findings.independence: Same Treasury series as finding 1, a different window (the period after the quarter). Investing.com's market snapshot of 2026-10-26 gives the 10y at 4.976%, consistent.

findings.finding: Short interest is crowded and still building into the print: 214.9M shares, 17.07% of float, 4.2 days to cover at the Sep 30 record date, up 13.7% from the prior settlement and roughly double the 9.28% of October 2025. The stock is 2% off its 52-week low with a +10.5 put skew, so a print that merely holds the FY profit guide has a squeeze mechanism.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On Oct 15, 2026 the stock rose 6.1% from an intraday 52-week low ($13.86) on no company news (Gotrade, TIKR), which shows how sensitive the stock is to short covering at these levels.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price rather than something it fails to reflect. The point is that it is one-sided: shorts at a multi-year high on a name already at its low skew the reaction to an in-line or better print upward. If the bear case were exhausted, short interest would be falling, not up 14% in one settlement.
findings.independence: Gotrade on the Oct 15 bounce (https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/sofi-sofi-stock-news-october-16-2026/), a different source.

findings.finding: Peer credit read is benign. Capital One's Q3 2026 release (Oct 20) shows a $225M loan reserve release and provision down $73M to $2.9B, and secondary coverage puts its domestic card NCO rate at 3.98% against 4.71% in Q2. SoFi's own personal-loan charge-off rate was 2.62% in Q2, down from 3.03% in Q1. Credit is therefore not the Q3 risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Credit has not been the line SOFI traded on in 2026. The negative reactions were driven by guidance and profit.
findings.why_not_priced: TipRanks' Oct 25 preview still cites 'growing credit risk from the loan business' as a headwind, so part of the market treats credit as a risk that the large-lender data does not show. If credit fear were gone, that framing would not appear in previews.
findings.independence: Proxy (card lender, not unsecured personal loans). SoFi's own Q2 charge-off trend in the Q2 8-K points the same way.

findings.finding: Personal-loan demand was healthy into Q3. Happen (formerly LendingClub) guided Q3 2026 originations to $3.20-3.35B against $3.1B in Q2 (up 29% year on year, above the top of its guide). Upstart's Q2 originations were up 50% year on year. This supports SoFi's lending volumes and the Loan Platform Business (which earned $143.3M in Q2).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: SoFi beat revenue in each of its last seven or more quarters (TipRanks). Revenue beats have not been rewarded in 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: this is July guidance, and SoFi's revenue beats are expected. Small on purpose. The open question is whether higher Q3 deposit costs cut what LPB buyers paid for loans, which is Goldman's point.
findings.independence: Proxy. Upstart Q2 2026 data via search; SoFi's own Q2 LPB figure is in the Q2 8-K.

findings.finding: Stablecoin and tokenized-deposit narrative: SOFIE (an interest-bearing tokenized deposit paying 4.40% that converts to SoFiUSD) launched Oct 22, and StoneX initiated at Buy with a $25 target, calling SoFi 'the most advanced bank-issued stablecoin franchise in the U.S.' The narrative cuts both ways: retail interest is a possible upside catalyst, while a 4.40% deposit yield points to rising deposit costs as the Fed hikes.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Sept 22 stablecoin settlement news took the stock to about $19 (TIKR), and the Oct 8 crypto-card launch in Mexico was followed by a slide to about $14. The narrative has not held.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public, and the two directions offset, so I size it at zero. It is filed so the judges can see it.

baseline_tension: The two negatives (rate-driven marks and the stretched H2 profit guide) agree with the +10.5 put skew and the -8.8% 20-day run-up, so they are largely priced. The positives (17% short interest and rising, the October rate reversal, benign peer credit) cut against the skew. The net is close to zero, and the move should be large in either direction.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (positioning; a sign that agrees with a strong skew is probably priced; a crowded short shrinks negatives): fair-value marks finding -1.5 to -1.0, guidance-ramp finding -1.5 to -1.0. Both negatives agree with the +10.5 skew and sit against 17% short interest that is still building.

Rule 5 (a macro proxy is filed small): the Capital One credit proxy went from +0.4 to +0.3. The rates-to-marks finding was already filed as a proxy and is not cut a second time beyond the rule 7 resize.

Rule 1 (this name sells its beats: -15.4% and -8.9% on revenue beats in 2026): no finding was cut for it. It moved p_up from 47 to 48 only through rule 7 together; print_vs_bar (+1.5) and expected_move (-0.36) are deliberately allowed to differ.
'Asking what was missed generates pessimism': I checked the set for sign balance and kept the positive findings (October rate reversal, short interest) at their draft sizes.
Left standing: the October rate reversal (+0.8), short interest (+1.0), LPB demand (+0.2), stablecoin (0.0).
